QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_9

question.text: An Interest Rate Cap is a series of:

explanation.text: The Logic: An interest rate cap is a series of interest rate call options called caplets. The buyer receives payment when the underlying interest rate exceeds the strike (cap) rate. Caps protect borrowers against rising rates. The Trap: An interest rate floor is a series of put options (floorlets). A collar combines a cap and a floor. Caps are protective instruments for floating-rate borrowers. Cross-Exam Context: Caps, floors, and collars are OTC interest rate options tested in Series IV and used by treasuries to manage floating rate exposure. Distributor's Pro-Tip: A borrower who buys a cap is effectively buying insurance against rising rates. The cap premium is the cost of this insurance — similar to option premium.
